cultural.vision_reason: The image shows an intricately carved wooden papahou (treasure box) with characteristic Māori rauponga spiral carving, openwork figures with haliotis-shell eyes — a well-documented Māori art form used to store precious items like huia feathers.

physical.title: box
physical.summary: Wooden treasure box, papahou : light brown, shallow, flat, rectangular, recessed for lid scalloped at ends. Sinuous-bodied, three-dimensional openwork composition of double figures projecting at each end. Bottom with central row of four wheku figures: middle pair male and female in sexual union; haliotis-shell eyes in outer figures and one such eye in female figure. Lid with high raised central ridge of openwork sinuous-bodied figures, head to head, with transverse median band of two smaller figures; three haliotis shell eyes in this composition. All figures decorated with rauponga and whakarare. Remainder of lid and box surface with rauponga spirals.
